messages:
sneha: FYI customer acme-fin reporting p99 spike on hosted /v1/generate around 09:00 UTC. p50 ~40ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~1.8s. Error rate small but 503s cluster during spikes. Started after batcher rollout at 08:50. dash: https://dash.redwood/cust/acme-fin/latency

ops-bot: [alert] route:/v1/generate p99 > 1.5s for tenant acme-fin (detected 09:02)

tariq: can we grab the continuous-batcher settings for that pool/tenant? suspect hold/grace interplay with many tiny requests.

maya: running command to fetch config:
```
redwoodctl get-pool-config --pool inference-prod-gpu-12 --tenant acme-fin --format json
```

maya: returned batcher config:
```
{"enable_continuous": true, "max_batch_size": 64, "grace_window_ms": 30, "hold_window_ms": 50, "max_wait_ms": 120}
```

liam: that hold_window is large relative to small prompts. If traffic is lots of 1-8 token requests we end up coalescing into big batches and hitting kernel scheduling + KV cache churn.

jon: also saw auth retry bursts around 08:52 in edge-proxy logs. Could be adding burstiness.

sneha: request size histogram for the route:
```
count: 12.3k
median tokens: 6
p90 tokens: 9
p99 tokens: 12
requests/sec: ~200
```

tariq: yep tiny-token heavy. hold_window=50ms will wait a lot, creating larger batches that take longer to execute and amplify tail. Need repro.

maya: lightweight repro script: `hey --concurrency 50 --qps 200 --post /v1/generate '{"prompt":"hi","tokens":6}' http://ingress.local`

liam: ran on canary. baseline (old config) p99 ~260ms. with current config p99 ~1.6s and we see flush reasons: hold_timeout + batch_size_reached. sample logs:
```
[09:01:23.456] node=gpux-7 batcher: queued=28 hold_elapsed_ms=51 reason=hold_timeout
[09:01:23.459] node=gpux-7 batcher: flush size=28 exec_ms=430
```

jon: kernel exec time higher for those big batches. KV cache churn + larger context switches per request.

mitigation ideas: reduce hold_window_ms to ~10ms, cap max_batch_size per-tenant (e.g., 16), or enable tiny-request fast-path that bypasses coalesce.

maya: canary change: set hold_window_ms=8 and max_batch_size=16 for acme-fin on 2 nodes. starting rollout.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout started by maya -> batcher-config/tenant-acme-fin (2 nodes)

maya: canary applied, watching metrics.

liam: 3m after canary p99 on canary nodes dropped from 1.6s -> ~350ms. 503s dropped too.

sneha: informed support and customer. they asked if auth/billing were root cause.

jon: auth retries caused burstiness but not root cause. root is batching amplification for tiny requests.

tariq: proposed next steps:
- rollback global faulty rollout (if still rolling) and pin safer defaults for latency-sensitive hosted pools: hold_window_ms <= 10, max_batch_size <= 32.
- implement adaptive heuristic: if median_tokens < 8 then reduce hold_window automatically.
- schedule tiny-request fast-path (bypass coalesce) in the 2-week roadmap.

sneha: filing follow-up ticket with repro, logs, config diffs. tagging CS and sales. ticket: https://issues.redwood/SE-4982

liam: PR to tighten defaults: set default hold_window_ms=10 for hosted pools. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/7321 (canary passed)

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout started for batcher-config defaults -> inference-prod (10 nodes)

tariq: also adding dashboard panels: "requests with tokens<=8 by tenant" + p99 by batch size to surface these faster.

sneha: scheduling 2-hour stabilization check at 11:15 UTC. will close after 2h stable.

liam: saved repro artifacts and profiles: /tmp/batcher_flame_acme_174765.log

sneha: thanks all. closing loop with customer. :thumbsup:
